question: Are there any pages with duplicate title tags?
answer: Yes, 233 searchable pages share a title with another page. Nearly all are recurring fund news releases that reuse one title each period, for example 'JOHN HANCOCK PREMIUM DIVIDEND FUND NOTICE TO SHAREHOLDERS - SOURCES OF DISTRIBUTION UNDER SECTION 19(a)', 'JOHN HANCOCK CLOSED-END FUNDS DECLARE MONTHLY DISTRIBUTIONS', the Tax-Advantaged Dividend Income Fund and Financial Opportunities Fund notices. Some differ only in letter case (Hedged Equity & Income Fund in upper case and in title case). The fix is to add the fund and the date or period to each title.
evidence: get_technical_checks duplicate_titles: findings_total 233 (ref fact:issue-30f1d464e657), each with also_on lists, for example the 2024/04, 2024/10, 2025/04, 2022/06, 2022/11 and 2023/03 premium-dividend-fund notices.
note: The also_on lists are long, so only about 14 findings fit in one call (paged).

question: How many pages have a noindex tag, and should any of them actually be indexed?
answer: 17 pages carry noindex, and they are all the Longer Healthier Better podcast episode pages (/individual/insights/longer-healthier-better-podcasts/...). They look like real editorial pages: each has a self-referencing canonical, its own title and meta description, and is in the knowledge base. So unless the noindex is deliberate (for example because the episodes are thin, at 261-362 main words), they are good candidates to make indexable. The docuseries page is not noindexed.
evidence: get_technical_checks robots_meta: 17 findings, all 'noindex', all podcast URLs (e.g. better-sleep-with-dr-matthew-walker, celebrating-a-decade-of-vitality-with-lindsay-hanson). get_page_facts better-sleep: canonical = own URL, meta description present, main_word_count 272, schema_types []. get_seo_issues noindex: 17 pages.
note: Whether they should be indexed is a judgement made from page facts; the engine gives no recommendation. X-Robots-Tag headers are not kept, so header noindex is not checked.

question: Give me a summary of the site's biggest SEO issues for Thursday's client meeting.
answer: For the 303 pages scraped (mostly news releases, help forms and podcasts), the biggest issues are: (1) 252 pages have no meta description and 284 titles are over 60 characters; (2) 233 pages share duplicate titles and 262 have more than one H1, usually the visible H1 plus a 'John Hancock Virtual Assistant' widget heading; (3) all 17 podcast episodes are noindexed and 4 of them have no H1; (4) 250 Article schemas lack author, dateModified and publisher.url, and 51 pages have no structured data; (5) internal links on every page appear only after scripts run or after a click (3,376 and 3,618 links), which crawlers that run no scripts cannot follow; (6) many fund notices are near-identical duplicates (similarity 0.999-1.0). There are no redirect chains, mixed content or broken internal links among the scraped pages.
evidence: get_seo_issues summary codes and counts: title_too_long 284, description_missing 252, noindex 17, h1_missing 4, h1_multiple 262, links_need_scripts 303 pages / 3376 items, links_behind_clicks 303 / 3618, images_alt_empty 302 / 1104, structured_data_recommended_missing 250, structured_data_missing 51. get_technical_checks: duplicate_titles 233, title_equals_h1 238, http_errors 2, redirects 0, broken_internal_links 0. get_structured_data: Article on 250 pages missing dateModified/author/publisher.url. find_similar_pages: pairs at similarity 1.0.
note: Caveat for the meeting: the scrape skipped the product sections (life insurance, annuities, LTC). Product-page SEO is unknown, and 9,888 internal links point to pages that were not fetched. There is no traffic or ranking data to rank the issues by impact.

question: Does the Vitality program get explained consistently across all the pages that mention it?
answer: Across the captured pages that mention it (press releases on Apple Watch, Oura and the correction, and the podcast episode 'Celebrating a decade of Vitality'), the program is described the same way: it 'rewards customers for the everyday things they do to live longer, healthier, better lives', and every page carries the same disclaimer that rewards are 'available only to the person insured under the eligible life insurance policy, may vary...'. One figure does not match: the 2023 Oura release says 'More than 30 million people in 40 markets', while the 2024 Apple Watch release says '42+ million people across 41+ markets'. That is a date difference, not a real contradiction. The main Vitality product pages were not scraped, so they could not be compared.
evidence: search_knowledge returned passages from only 3-4 pages. get_page on /about-us/news/john-hancock/2024/11/john-hancock-adds-new-apple-watch-series-10-to-its-vitality-program, /2023/05/john-hancock-announces-collaboration-with-oura, /2024/12/correction-john-hancock and /individual/insights/longer-healthier-better-podcasts/celebrating-a-decade-of-vitality-with-lindsay-hanson.
